Skills can inject content at this point if they hook into before_agent_start via the extension system.

Caveman extension vs skill interaction: caveman-enforcer.ts injects via `before_agent_start` hook (line 288-292), appending cavemanPrompt(level) to systemPrompt. agent-team.ts extension (disabled in settings.json) loads agent-skills/*.md via `readAgentSkills()` (line 243-258) and formats them into system prompt with `formatAgentSkillsBlock()` when dispatching agents. Caveman extension runs in main pi session; agent-team dispatched agents run with `--no-extensions` (line 508, 1421) which disables caveman-enforcer for dispatched agents.

Caveman extension APPENDS style rules via before_agent_start, not prepends. Multiple extensions inject after: goal-tracker, cron, auto-delegate, enforce-subagent. Unknown runtime hook order may dilute caveman directive strength. Extension uses return { systemPrompt: ... } which may short-circuit chain.

Pi framework extension injection: before_agent_start returns systemPrompt string, which becomes the first message sent to LLM (role: "system" or "developer"). Extensions control prepend/append order via string concatenation. Caveman currently appends at end (~1,500-4,000 char base prompt) - weaker enforcement. Prepending would be stronger. Custom messages (role: "custom") are filtered out before LLM call - only for UI/display, not model behavior.
